artworks.title: Apotheosis of Julius Caesar
artworks.description: Laguerre's Chatsworth ceiling: Julius Caesar lifted toward the gods — Baroque apotheosis for the dictator Ovid ends as a star.

artworks.title: Murder and Deification of Julius Caesar
artworks.description: Rijksmuseum print: the Ides murder paired with Caesar's deification — reception's hinge between Curia steel and celestial ascent.

artworks.title: Augustus Denarius with Sidus Iulium (RIC I 37a)
artworks.description: Silver denarius: Augustus' coinage of the Julian star — the sidus Iulium that Romans read as Caesar's soul ascending.

artworks.title: Comet Caesar (Roman denarius)
artworks.description: Roman denarius reverse with Caesar's comet — the daylight omen Augustan propaganda and Ovid's Metamorphoses XV made proof of apotheosis.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Book XV closes the poem with Venus bearing Julius Caesar to the stars — the comet as Rome's last metamorphosis under Augustus.

popCulture.title: Caesar's Comet
popCulture.description: The daylight comet Romans read as Caesar's soul ascending — Ovid's celestial proof and Augustan propaganda's brightest omen.

popCulture.title: Julius Caesar (play)
popCulture.creator: William Shakespeare
popCulture.description: Shakespeare's tragedy ends before Ovid's star, but the murdered dictator and the heirs who claim his name keep the apotheosis in the culture's ear.

popCulture.title: Augustus
popCulture.description: The heir who guards the earth while Caesar becomes a star — Ovid's closing couplet of empire and metamorphosis.
